feed.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?

entry.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
entry.summary:
When designing user interfaces for cryptocurrency wallets, the placement of advanced options such as address type selection is crucial. Providing both traditional SegWit (p2wpkh) and taproot address types can introduce confusion if not handled carefully, especially for users who are primarily interested in simple transactions like sending or receiving bitcoin from an exchange or through peer-to-peer platforms. For most mainstream users, p2wpkh addresses have become the prevailing standard, as demonstrated by the current output type distribution data available at [https://mainnet.observer/charts/output-type-distribution-count/](https://mainnet.observer/charts/output-type-distribution-count/).
Taproot offers notable technical benefits, but these advantages may not be directly relevant to the majority of everyday users. Mainstream wallet implementations that do not focus on complex scripting capabilities would benefit from defaulting to p2wpkh addresses, ensuring smooth and familiar experiences for general use cases. This approach simplifies the user's journey and minimizes the potential for confusion.
Documentation and support resources play a significant role in shaping user perceptions and understanding. For instance, the [Gem Wallet Bitcoin support page](https://gemwallet.com/bitcoin-wallet/) does not reference `bc1p`-type taproot addresses. This omission could contribute to misconceptions among users, such as believing that taproot addresses are non-functional or unsupported within certain wallets. Comprehensive documentation should clearly explain all supported address formats to enhance transparency and foster user confidence.
